```sh
nub run --filter=@zod/docs dev
```

npm install zod @zod/mini

### Install Nub v0.8.3

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Installs Nub version 0.8.3, which manages dependencies, scripts, and Node versions. Restart the shell after installation so Nub is added to PATH.

```sh

### Install zod@^4.5.0 to use z.compile()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Install the Zod version that provides the compiler. After installing, call z.compile() on hot-path schemas or import "zod/compile" at your entry point. Bundles that never call z.compile() or import zod/compile are tree-shaken and pay no bundle-size cost.

```sh
npm install zod@^4.5.0
```

### Inspect materialized schema metadata properties on first read

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-6.mdx

Shows how metadata keys like .minLength start as prototype getters and materialize as own properties only after they are read.

```ts
const s = z.string().min(3).max(9);

Object.keys(s); // 4.5: ["def", "type", "format", "minLength", "maxLength"] — 4.6: ["def", "type"]
s.minLength;    // 3 in both
Object.keys(s); // 4.6: ["def", "type", "minLength"]
```

--------------------------------

### Control refinement execution with when parameter (Zod Mini)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Use the when parameter to run the refinement only when there are no issues with password or confirmPassword. An error on anotherField will still prevent the password check from running in this example.

```ts
const schema = z
  .object({
    password: z.string().check(z.minLength(8)),
    confirmPassword: z.string(),
    anotherField: z.string(),
  })
  .check(z.refine((data) => data.password === data.confirmPassword, {
    message: "Passwords do not match",
    path: ["confirmPassword"],

    when(payload) { // [!code ++]
      // no issues with `password` or `confirmPassword` // [!code ++]
      return payload.issues.every((iss) => { // [!code ++]
        const firstPathEl = iss.path?.[0]; // [!code ++]
        return firstPathEl !== "password" && firstPathEl !== "confirmPassword"; // [!code ++]
      }); // [!code ++]
    },  // [!code ++]
  }));

schema.parse({
  password: "asdf",
  confirmPassword: "asdf",
  anotherField: 1234 // ❌ this error will prevent the password check from running
});
```

### Base Recipe object schema for pick/omit/partial examples

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Initial `Recipe` schema used by the following `.pick()`, `.omit()`, `.partial()`, and `.exactPartial()` examples.

```ts
const Recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string().optional(),
  ingredients: z.array(z.string()),
});
// { title: string; description?: string | undefined; ingredients: string[] }
```

### Install external parser using z.withParser()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-6.mdx

Applies an externally generated parser or type guard to a schema to avoid new Function execution under strict Content Security Policies. The parser must return the processed schema output or return z.INVALID to delegate error handling to Zod.

```typescript
const Player = z.object({ username: z.string(), xp: z.number() });

// isPlayer is a type guard your build step generated
const Fast = z.withParser(Player, (input) =>
  isPlayer(input) ? { username: input.username, xp: input.xp } : z.INVALID
);
```

--------------------------------

### Use .check() with Zod Mini to create multiple issues

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Zod Mini version of the .check() example. It demonstrates pushing a too_big issue and a custom duplicate issue with continue: true, giving full control over issue objects.

```ts
const UniqueStringArray = z.array(z.string()).check((ctx) => {
  // full control of issue objects
  if (ctx.value.length > 3) {
    ctx.issues.push({
      code: "too_big",
      maximum: 3,
      origin: "array",
      inclusive: true,
      message: "Too many items 😡",
      input: ctx.value
    });
  }

// create multiple issues in one refinement
  if (ctx.value.length !== new Set(ctx.value).size) {
    ctx.issues.push({
      code: "custom",
      message: `No duplicates allowed.`,
      input: ctx.value,
      continue: true // make this issue continuable (default: false)
    });
  }
});
```

### Parse with a compiled Zod schema

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Compiled schemas are used exactly like the original schema. Calling .parse() on the compiled schema is roughly 9x faster for this example.

```ts
Player.parse({ ... });
CompiledPlayer.parse({ ... }); // ~9x faster
```

const Point = z.object({

### Enable compile-by-default with import "zod/compile"

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Import "zod/compile" in your application entry point (or before any schemas are defined) to make all declared schemas self-compile on first use. Compilation is lazy, so only schemas you actually parse with get compiled.

```ts
// in your entrypoint (or before any schemas are defined)
import "zod/compile";
```

### Register metadata with z.globalRegistry using .register()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/metadata.mdx

Use .register(z.globalRegistry, metadata) to attach metadata such as id, title, description, and examples to a schema. This is useful for JSON Schema generation or other metadata-driven tasks.

```typescript
import * as z from "zod";

const emailSchema = z.email().register(z.globalRegistry, { 
  id: "email_address",
  title: "Email address",
  description: "Your email address",
  examples: ["first.last@example.com"]
});
```

### Push initial branch with explicit refspec and verify output

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/AGENTS.md

Use an explicit refspec on the initial push to ensure the remote ref targets a new branch instead of main. Verify that the output displays a new branch creation rather than pointing to main.

```bash
# Always use a refspec on the initial push so the remote ref name is unambiguous.
git push -u origin <branch>:refs/heads/<branch>
```

```text
* [new branch]      <branch> -> <branch>
```

### Add, check, get, remove, and clear schemas in a registry

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/metadata.mdx

Register a schema with metadata, then use has, get, remove, and clear to manage registry entries.

```ts
const mySchema = z.string();

myRegistry.add(mySchema, { description: "A cool schema!"});
myRegistry.has(mySchema); // => true
myRegistry.get(mySchema); // => { description: "A cool schema!" }
myRegistry.remove(mySchema);
myRegistry.clear(); // wipe registry
```

### Define a fixed-length tuple with z.tuple

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Tuples specify a different schema for each index; infer the type to get a fixed-length tuple type.

```ts
const MyTuple = z.tuple([
  z.string(),
  z.number(),
  z.boolean()
]);

type MyTuple = z.infer<typeof MyTuple>;
// [string, number, boolean]
```

### Define and parse schemas using @zod/mini

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/mini/README.md

Import @zod/mini to define an object schema with checks and parse input data.

```ts
import * as z from "@zod/mini";

const User = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
  age: z.number().check(z.int(), z.positive()),
});

z.parse(User, { name: "Colin", age: 30 });
```

### Use async and safe variants of decode

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Demonstrates the return types of synchronous, asynchronous, and safe execution variants for decoding.

```ts
stringToDate.decode("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => Date

stringToDate.decodeAsync("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => Promise<Date>

stringToDate.safeDecode("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => { success: true, data: Date } | { success: false, error: ZodError }

stringToDate.safeDecodeAsync("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); 
// => Promise<{ success: true, data: Date } | { success: false, error: ZodError }>
```

### Normalize URLs with new URL()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

The normalize flag overwrites the input with the normalized URL returned by new URL(). This example shows the normalized href output.

```typescript
new URL("HTTP://ExAmPle.com:80/./a/../b?X=1#f oo").href
// => "http://example.com/b?X=1#f%20oo"
```

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Use z.templateLiteral to build a template literal schema from string literals and schemas. The example produces the type `hello, ${string}!`.

```ts
const schema = z.templateLiteral([ "hello, ", z.string(), "!" ]);
// `hello, ${string}!`
```

### Extract allowed literal values with .values (Zod)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

In Zod, read the .values property to get the set of allowed values from a literal schema. Zod Mini has no equivalent.

```ts
colors.values; // => Set<"red" | "green" | "blue">
```

```ts
// no equivalent
```

--------------------------------

### Define a bidirectional transformation codec with z.codec()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Create a codec by supplying an input schema, output schema, and explicit decode/encode transform functions.

```ts
const stringToDate = z.codec(
  z.iso.datetime(),  // input schema: ISO date string
  z.date(),          // output schema: Date object
  {
    decode: (isoString) => new Date(isoString), // ISO string → Date
    encode: (date) => date.toISOString(),       // Date → ISO string
  }
);
```

--------------------------------

### .exactPartial()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Identical to .partial(), but wraps each field in exactOptional() instead of optional().

```APIDOC
## .exactPartial()

### Description
Identical to .partial(), but wraps each field in exactOptional() instead of optional().

### Method
.exactPartial()

### Parameters
None.

### Examples

#### Zod
```ts
const Recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string().optional(),
  ingredients: z.array(z.string()),
});
// { title: string; description?: string | undefined; ingredients: string[] }

const PartialRecipe = Recipe.exactPartial();
// { title?: string; description?: string | undefined; ingredients?: string[] }
```

#### Zod Mini
```ts
const Recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string().optional(),
  ingredients: z.array(z.string()),
});
// { title: string; description?: string | undefined; ingredients: string[] }

const PartialRecipe = z.exactPartial(Recipe);
// { title?: string; description?: string | undefined; ingredients?: string[] }
```
```

### Configure peerDependencies to support Zod 3 and Zod 4

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Widen your package.json peer dependency to span both Zod 3 and Zod 4 ranges. The zod/v4 subpath is available starting in version 3.25.0.

```json
// package.json
{
  // ...
  "peerDependencies": {
    "zod": "^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0"
  }
}
```

### Define a fallback value with .catch() in Zod

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Use `.catch()` to return a fallback value when validation fails. In this example, parsing "tuna" returns 42 instead of throwing.

```ts
const numberWithCatch = z.number().catch(42);

numberWithCatch.parse(5); // => 5
numberWithCatch.parse("tuna"); // => 42
```

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/introducing-z-compile.mdx

Use the Node.js --import flag for ESM or --require for CommonJS to guarantee compilation is enabled before any module defines a schema.

```sh
node --import zod/compile app.js   # ESM
node --require zod/compile app.cjs # CommonJS
```

### Invoke standard ZodType instance methods

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/packages/zod.mdx

Demonstrates parsing, refinement, wrapper, metadata, and utility methods available on all ZodType instances.

```typescript
import * as z from "zod";

const mySchema = z.string();

// parsing
mySchema.parse(data);
mySchema.safeParse(data);
mySchema.parseAsync(data);
mySchema.safeParseAsync(data);


// refinements
mySchema.refine(refinementFunc);
mySchema.superRefine(refinementFunc); // deprecated, use `.check()`
mySchema.overwrite(overwriteFunc);

// wrappers
mySchema.optional();
mySchema.nonoptional();
mySchema.nullable();
mySchema.nullish();
mySchema.default(defaultValue);
mySchema.array();
mySchema.or(otherSchema);
mySchema.transform(transformFunc);
mySchema.catch(catchValue);
mySchema.pipe(otherSchema);
mySchema.readonly();

// metadata and registries
mySchema.register(registry, metadata);
mySchema.describe(description);
mySchema.meta(metadata);

// utilities
mySchema.check(checkOrFunction);
mySchema.clone(def);
mySchema.brand<T>();
mySchema.isOptional(); // boolean
mySchema.isNullable(); // boolean
```

### TypeScript discriminated union type narrowing example

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Shows how TypeScript narrows a discriminated union based on the status discriminator key. Use as reference for the type behavior Zod's z.discriminatedUnion mirrors.

```typescript
type MyResult =
  | { status: "success"; data: string }
  | { status: "failed"; error: string };

function handleResult(result: MyResult){
  if(result.status === "success"){
    result.data; // string
  } else {
    result.error; // string
  }
}
```

### Create multiple issues with superRefine (Zod)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Unlike .refine, .superRefine() can create multiple issues using Zod's internal issue types. This example adds a too_big issue and a custom duplicate issue.

```ts
const UniqueStringArray = z.array(z.string()).superRefine((val, ctx) => {
  if (val.length > 3) {
    ctx.addIssue({
      code: "too_big",
      maximum: 3,
      origin: "array",
      inclusive: true,
      message: "Too many items 😡",
      input: val,
    });
  }

  if (val.length !== new Set(val).size) {
    ctx.addIssue({
      code: "custom",
      message: `No duplicates allowed.`,
      input: val,
    });
  }
});


```

--------------------------------

### Handling Absent Keys and Optionality in Zod

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/wiki/optionality.md

Demonstrates runtime parsing and static typing behavior for transforms, coerce/unknown schemas, exactOptional modifiers, and preprocess pipes when keys are absent or undefined.

```typescript
z.object({ a: z.unknown().transform((v) => String(v ?? "X")).pipe(z.string()) }).parse({})
// → THROW  (outer pipe.optin = inner pipe.optin = unknown.optin = undefined — transform is
//   on the OUT side of the inner pipe, which is on the IN side of the outer pipe; the leading
//   `z.unknown()` drives optin and it's not "optional")
//
//   Compare to z.preprocess(fn, T):
//     z.preprocess(fn, T) === pipe(transform(fn), T)         — transform IS def.in of the only pipe
//     z.unknown().transform(fn).pipe(T) === pipe(pipe(unknown, transform), T)  — there's an
//                                                                                inner pipe with
//                                                                                z.unknown() on
//                                                                                the in side
//
//   Preprocess accepts absent because its leading position is the transform itself.
//   The unknown.transform.pipe(T) shape doesn't, because its leading position is z.unknown().
//   If you want preprocess-like absence-handling, use z.preprocess; if you specifically want
//   strict input typing on the leading slot, the unknown.transform.pipe shape gives that.

// === Coerce / unknown / any (intentionally strict on absent) ===

z.object({ a: z.coerce.string() }).parse({})
// → THROW  (coerce.string.optin = undefined; object rejects absent key)

z.object({ a: z.unknown() }).parse({})
// → THROW  (unknown.optin = undefined; soundness fix from 4.4)

z.object({ a: z.any() }).parse({})
// → THROW  (same)

// === exactOptional (delegates instead of short-circuiting) ===

z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().exactOptional() }).parse({})
// → {}  (absent + middle rung: the object drops what coerce made of undefined)

z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().exactOptional() }).parse({ a: undefined })
// → { a: "undefined" }  (present: the inner runs and its answer stands)

z.object({ a: z.string().exactOptional() }).parse({ a: undefined })
// → THROW  (present: string rejects undefined, and the object surfaces it)

z.object({ a: z.string().default("x").exactOptional() }).parse({})
// → { a: "x" }  (top rung substitutes, so the gate doesn't fire)

z.tuple([z.string(), z.coerce.string().exactOptional()]).parse(["x"])
// → ["x"]  (the tuple analog: truncate rather than materialize)

// === Static type vs runtime divergence ===

z.input<typeof z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") })>
// → { a: string }   — `a` is required at the type level

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") }).parse({})
// → { a: "c" }      — but accepts {} at runtime

z.input<typeof z.object({ a: z.preprocess(fn, T) })>
// → { a: <transform's input type> }   — `a` is required at the type level

z.object({ a: z.preprocess(fn, T) }).parse({})
// → { a: fn(undefined) }   — accepts {} at runtime
```

### Create an async function with .implementAsync()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Use .implementAsync() to create an async function that returns a Promise.

```ts
const computeTrimmedLengthAsync = MyFunction.implementAsync(
  async (input) => input.trim().length
);

computeTrimmedLengthAsync("sandwich"); // => Promise<8>
```

--------------------------------

### Compare prefault and default with mutating refinements

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

`.prefault()` passes the value through refinements like `.trim()` and `.toUpperCase()`, while `.default()` returns the value unchanged. Use prefault when you want the fallback to be processed.

```ts
const a = z.string().trim().toUpperCase().prefault("  tuna  ");
a.parse(undefined); // => "TUNA"

const b = z.string().trim().toUpperCase().default("  tuna  ");
b.parse(undefined); // => "  tuna  "
```

--------------------------------

### import "zod/compile"

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/compile.mdx

Enables compilation globally. Every schema constructed after this import is compiled automatically the first time it parses. Compilation is lazy, so only schemas actually parsed get compiled. This import is for applications, not libraries.

```APIDOC
## import "zod/compile"

### Description
Enables compilation globally. Every schema constructed *after* this import is compiled automatically the first time it parses. Compilation is lazy, so only the schemas you actually parse with get compiled. This import is for applications, not libraries.

### Usage
```ts
import "zod/compile"; // must come before modules that define schemas
import * as z from "zod";

const schema = z.object({ name: z.string() });
schema.parse({ name: "ok" }); // compiled on first parse
```

### CLI Flags
```sh
node --import zod/compile app.js   # ESM
node --require zod/compile app.cjs # CommonJS
```

### Preload Configuration
Set `preload` in `bunfig.toml` or `nub.jsonc`.

```jsonc title="nub.jsonc"
{
  "preload": ["zod/compile"]
}
```
```

### Create multiple issues with z.superRefine in check (Zod Mini)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

In Zod Mini, use z.superRefine inside .check() to create multiple issues using Zod's internal issue types. This example adds a too_big issue and a custom duplicate issue.

```ts
const UniqueStringArray = z.array(z.string()).check(
  z.superRefine((val, ctx) => {
    if (val.length > 3) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "too_big",
        maximum: 3,
        origin: "array",
        inclusive: true,
        message: "Too many items 😡",
        input: val,
      });
    }

    if (val.length !== new Set(val).size) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "custom",
        message: `No duplicates allowed.`,
        input: val,
      });
    }
  })
);
```

### Use the .transform() convenience method in Zod

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Shorthand for piping a schema into a transform. There is no equivalent in Zod Mini.

```ts
const stringToLength = z.string().transform(val => val.length); 
```

### Parse values with z.coerce.string schema

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

The coerced string schema converts various input types to strings. For example, parsing 42 returns "42", true returns "true", and null returns "null".

```ts
const schema = z.coerce.string();

schema.parse("tuna");    // => "tuna"
schema.parse(42);        // => "42"
schema.parse(true);      // => "true"
schema.parse(null);      // => "null"
```

### Validate File instances with z.file() in Zod Mini

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

In Zod Mini, apply file constraints via .check() with z.minSize, z.maxSize, and z.mime. Sizes are in bytes and mime accepts a single type or an array.

```ts
const fileSchema = z.file();

fileSchema.check(z.minSize(10_000)); // minimum .size (bytes)
fileSchema.check(z.maxSize(1_000_000)); // maximum .size (bytes)
fileSchema.check(z.mime("image/png")); // MIME type
fileSchema.check(z.mime(["image/png", "image/jpeg"])); // multiple MIME types
```

--------------------------------

### Register metadata with .meta() or z.globalRegistry

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/json-schema.mdx

Registers metadata fields such as title and description on a Zod schema to include them in the generated JSON Schema.

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

// `.meta()` is a convenience method for registering a schema in `z.globalRegistry`
const emailSchema = z.string().meta({ 
  title: "Email address",
  description: "Your email address",
});

z.toJSONSchema(emailSchema);
// => { type: "string", title: "Email address", description: "Your email address", ... } 
```

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

// `.meta()` is a convenience method for registering a schema in `z.globalRegistry`
const emailSchema = z.string().register(z.globalRegistry, { 
  title: "Email address",
  description: "Your email address",
});

z.toJSONSchema(emailSchema);
// => { type: "string", title: "Email address", description: "Your email address", ... } 
```

--------------------------------

### Boolean coercion with z.coerce.boolean

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Any truthy value is coerced to true, and any falsy value is coerced to false. For example, parsing "tuna", "true", "false", 1, and [] all return true; parsing 0, "", undefined, and null return false.

```ts
const schema = z.coerce.boolean(); // Boolean(input)

schema.parse("tuna"); // => true
schema.parse("true"); // => true
schema.parse("false"); // => true
schema.parse(1); // => true
schema.parse([]); // => true

schema.parse(0); // => false
schema.parse(""); // => false
schema.parse(undefined); // => false
schema.parse(null); // => false
```

Upgrade to Zod 4.5 or later to take advantage of reduced memory footprint enhancements.

```sh
npm upgrade zod@latest
```

### Use .check() to create multiple issues in one refinement

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

The .check() API provides low-level control over issue objects and allows creating multiple issues in a single refinement. Use it when you need full control over issue generation or performance-sensitive paths. The example shows pushing a too_big issue and a custom duplicate issue with continue: true.

```ts
const UniqueStringArray = z.array(z.string()).check((ctx) => {
  if (ctx.value.length > 3) {
    // full control of issue objects
    ctx.issues.push({
      code: "too_big",
      maximum: 3,
      origin: "array",
      inclusive: true,
      message: "Too many items 😡",
      input: ctx.value
    });
  }

  // create multiple issues in one refinement
  if (ctx.value.length !== new Set(ctx.value).size) {
    ctx.issues.push({
      code: "custom",
      message: `No duplicates allowed.`,
      input: ctx.value,
      continue: true // make this issue continuable (default: false)
    });
  }
});
```

### Simple string transforms (Zod Mini)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Equivalent string transforms in Zod Mini using .check() with z.trim, z.toLowerCase, z.toUpperCase, and z.normalize.

```ts
z.string().check(z.trim()); // trim whitespace
z.string().check(z.toLowerCase()); // toLowerCase
z.string().check(z.toUpperCase()); // toUpperCase
z.string().check(z.normalize()); // normalize unicode characters
```

### Project schema input and output with z.input() and z.output()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-5.mdx

Useful for validating the two halves of a codec independently. This is a no-op on schemas that do not contain codecs or pipes.

```ts
const isoDate = z.codec(z.iso.datetime(), z.date(), {
  decode: (s) => new Date(s),
  encode: (d) => d.toISOString(),
});

const Event = z.object({ name: z.string(), at: isoDate });

z.input(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }); // ✅
z.output(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: new Date() });            // ✅
```

Use z.nullish to make a schema both optional and nullable.

const nullishYoda = z.nullish(z.literal("yoda"));
```

const res = await fetch("/api/user");

### Evaluate optionality interactions with catch, default, prefault, preprocess, and transform

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/wiki/optionality.md

Details the evaluation results and optin mechanics for schema combinations using catch, default, prefault, preprocess, transform, and optional modifiers. Illustrates how different modifiers resolve undefined inputs, transform pipelines, and object property omission.

```typescript
// === Catch ===

z.string().catch("c").parse(undefined)
// → "c"  (catch fires on string(undefined) failure; nothing outer to override it)

z.string().catch("c").parse(123)
// → "c"  (catch fires on string(123) failure)

z.string().catch("c").optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (catch.optin = "optional", not "defaulted", so optional yields undefined without running it)

z.string().catch("c").optional().parse("hi")
// → "hi"  (input defined, so optional just runs the inner)

z.string().catch("c").transform((s) => s + "!").optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (pipe.optin = catch.optin = "optional"; optional yields undefined)

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") }).parse({})
// → { a: "c" }  (catch.optin = "optional" runtime; obj invokes catch with undefined; catch fires)

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") }).parse({ a: undefined })
// → { a: "c" }  (key present with undefined; catch fires on string(undefined))

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c").optional() }).parse({})
// → {}  (key absent; optional sees optin = "optional", not "defaulted", so yields undefined; obj omits)

// === Default ===

z.string().default("d").parse(undefined)
// → "d"  (default short-circuits on undef input, returns d directly)

z.string().default("d").optional().parse(undefined)
// → "d"  (default.optin = "defaulted"; optional runs it and respects the result)

z.object({ a: z.string().default("d") }).parse({})
// → { a: "d" }  (obj asks optin !== undefined; invokes default; short-circuits to d)

// === Prefault ===

z.string().prefault("p").parse(undefined)
// → "p"  (prefault substitutes, runs inner string("p") which succeeds)

z.string().prefault("p").optional().parse(undefined)
// → "p"  (prefault.optin = "defaulted" — it answers the absence, so optional respects it)

// === Preprocess ===

z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()).parse(undefined)
// → "X"  (preprocess fn produces "X", inner string accepts)

z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()).optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (pipe.optin = transform.optin = "optional"; optional yields undefined, fn never runs)

z.object({ a: z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()) }).parse({})
// → { a: "X" }  (preprocess.optin = "optional" via transform; obj invokes; fn runs)

z.object({ a: z.preprocess((v) => v ?? "X", z.string()).optional() }).parse({})
// → {}  (optional sees "optional", not "defaulted"; yields undefined without running the fn; obj omits)

z.object({ a: z.preprocess((v) => v, z.string().optional()) }).parse({})
// → {}  (inner-optional preprocess; #5917/#5929 path)

// === Default feeding a transform (the #6321 shape) ===

z.string().default("").transform((v) => (v ? v.split(",") : [])).optional().parse(undefined)
// → []  (pipe.optin = def.in.optin = default.optin = "defaulted"; optional runs it and respects)
//   4.4.3-4.4.x: was undefined, because transform flagged every invocation as a fallback

z.object({ a: z.string().default("").transform((v) => v.length) }).partial().parse({})
// → { a: 0 }  (.partial() wraps in optional; the top rung carries through the pipe)

// === Transform ===

z.string().transform((s) => s + "!").parse("hi")
// → "hi!"

z.string().transform((s) => s + "!").parse(undefined)
// → THROW  (string rejects undef before transform runs)

z.transform((v) => v ?? "X").parse(undefined)
// → "X"  (transform fn runs on undef, returns "X")

z.transform((v) => v ?? "X").optional().parse(undefined)
// → undefined  (transform.optin = "optional"; optional yields undefined, fn never runs)

z.object({ a: z.transform((v) => v ?? "X") }).parse({})
// → { a: "X" }  (transform.optin = "optional" runtime; obj invokes transform with undef)

z.object({ a: z.string().transform((s) => s + "!") }).parse({})
// → THROW  (pipe.optin = string.optin = undefined — transform on OUT side doesn't drive optin)
```

z.file();

### .describe()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/metadata.mdx

A shorthand method for registering a schema in z.globalRegistry with just a description field. The .meta() method is the recommended approach.

```APIDOC
## .describe()

### Description
A shorthand method for registering a schema in `z.globalRegistry` with just a `description` field. The `.meta()` method is the recommended approach.

### Method
`.describe(description: string)`

### Parameters
- **description** (string) - Required - The description to register.

### Examples

#### Zod
```ts
const emailSchema = z.email();
emailSchema.describe("An email address");

// equivalent to
emailSchema.meta({ description: "An email address" });
```

#### Zod Mini
```ts
const emailSchema = z.email().check(z.describe("An email address"));

// equivalent to
z.email().check(z.meta({ description: "An email address" }));
```
```

### Make all fields exact-optional with exactPartial (Zod Mini)

Zod Mini equivalent using the standalone `z.exactPartial()` function, wrapping each field in `exactOptional()`.

```ts
const PartialRecipe = z.exactPartial(Recipe);
// { title?: string; description?: string | undefined; ingredients?: string[] }

### Create a pipe with z.string().pipe() in Zod

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Chains a string schema into a transform using the .pipe() method. Parsing "hello" returns 5.

```ts
const stringToLength = z.string().pipe(z.transform(val => val.length));

stringToLength.parse("hello"); // => 5
```

### Convert file schema with size and MIME constraints

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/json-schema.mdx

Converts size and MIME checks on `z.file()` to `minLength`, `maxLength`, and `contentMediaType` in JSON Schema.

```ts
z.file().min(1).max(1024 * 1024).mime("image/png");
// => {
//   type: "string",
//   format: "binary",
//   contentEncoding: "binary",
//   contentMediaType: "image/png",
//   minLength: 1,
//   maxLength: 1048576,
// }
```

### Use the .properties() method on z.instanceof

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

In Zod, z.instanceof also has a .properties() method that spreads the same check and narrows the inferred type.

```ts
const okResponse = z.instanceof(Response).properties({
  status: z.number().min(200).max(299),
  redirected: z.literal(false),
});

type OkResponse = z.infer<typeof okResponse>;
// => Response & { status: number; redirected: false }
```

--------------------------------

### Accept minute and second precision with a z.union of z.iso.datetime()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

No single precision covers both minute and second precision, so union the default schema with precision: -1. Unqualified datetimes remain rejected.

```ts
const mixed = z.union([z.iso.datetime(), z.iso.datetime({ precision: -1 })]);
mixed.parse("2020-01-01T06:15Z"); // ✅
mixed.parse("2020-01-01T06:15:00.123Z"); // ✅
mixed.parse("2020-01-01T06:15"); // ❌ (still qualified-only)
```

--------------------------------

### Use z.exactOptional() to disallow explicit undefined (Zod Mini)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

In Zod Mini, use z.exactOptional() to allow an absent key without allowing an explicit undefined. Parsing { name: undefined } succeeds, while { nick: undefined } fails.

```ts
const User = z.object({
  name: z.optional(z.string()),
  nick: z.exactOptional(z.string()),
});
// { name?: string | undefined; nick?: string }

z.parse(User, { name: undefined }); // ✅
z.parse(User, { nick: undefined }); // ❌
```

--------------------------------

### z.input() / z.output()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-5.mdx

Projects a schema onto its input or output side, useful for validating the two halves of a codec independently. This is a no-op on schemas not containing codecs/pipes.

```APIDOC
## z.input() / z.output()

### Description
Projects a schema onto its input or output side, useful for validating the two halves of a codec independently. This is a no-op on schemas not containing codecs/pipes.

### Method
z.input(schema)
z.output(schema)

### Parameters
- **schema** (ZodType) - Required - The schema to project onto its input or output side.

### Example
```ts
const isoDate = z.codec(z.iso.datetime(), z.date(), {
  decode: (s) => new Date(s),
  encode: (d) => d.toISOString(),
});

const Event = z.object({ name: z.string(), at: isoDate });

z.input(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }); // ✅
z.output(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: new Date() });            // ✅
```
```

--------------------------------

### Check multiple properties with z.properties (Zod Mini)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Zod Mini variant of checking several Response properties at once, using z.minimum and z.maximum instead of min/max. The 404 response fails on status.

```ts
const okResponse = z.instanceof(Response).check(
  ...z.properties({
    status: z.number().check(z.minimum(200), z.maximum(299)),
    redirected: z.literal(false),
  })
);

okResponse.parse(new Response("ok")); // ✅
okResponse.parse(new Response("", { status: 404 })); // ❌ status
```

--------------------------------

### Parse, decode, and encode with standard Zod schema methods

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Execute forward parsing and decoding or backward encoding on standard Zod schemas where input and output types match.

```ts
const schema = z.string();

type Input = z.input<typeof schema>;    // string
type Output = z.output<typeof schema>;  // string

schema.parse("asdf");   // => "asdf"
schema.decode("asdf");  // => "asdf"
schema.encode("asdf");  // => "asdf"
```

Zod Mini equivalent using the standalone `z.pick()` function to select keys from an object schema.

```ts
const JustTheTitle = z.pick(Recipe, { title: true });
```

.describe() is a shorthand for registering a description in z.globalRegistry. It is equivalent to calling .meta({ description: ... }).

const emailSchema = z.email();

### Invert a codec using z.invertCodec() in Zod Mini

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Derive the reverse codec and invoke standalone z.decode() and z.encode() functions on the inverted schema.

```ts
const dateToString = z.invertCodec(stringToDate);

z.decode(dateToString, new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"));
// => string

z.encode(dateToString, "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z");
// => Date
```

### Supporting Zod and Zod Mini with zod/v4/core

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Import from "zod/v4/core" in library code to access shared base interfaces, parsing utilities, and internal schema definitions.

```typescript
// library code
import * as z4 from "zod/v4/core";

export function acceptObjectSchema<T extends z4.$ZodObject>(schema: T){
  // parse data
  z4.parse(schema, { /* somedata */});
  // inspect internals
  schema._zod.def.shape;
}
```

### Set schema constraints: .nonempty(), .min(), .max(), .size()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Set schemas can be further constrained with utility methods to enforce size requirements. In Zod, use .nonempty(), .min(), .max(), and .size() directly on the set schema. In Zod Mini, use .check() with z.minSize(), z.maxSize(), and z.size().

```APIDOC
## Set schema constraints

### Description
Set schemas can be further constrained with utility methods to enforce size requirements. In Zod, use .nonempty(), .min(), .max(), and .size() directly on the set schema. In Zod Mini, use .check() with z.minSize(), z.maxSize(), and z.size().

### Method
Set schema constraint methods

### Parameters
- **nonempty()** - No parameters - Must contain at least 1 item.
- **min(n)** - **n** (number) - Required - Must contain n or more items.
- **max(n)** - **n** (number) - Required - Must contain n or fewer items.
- **size(n)** - **n** (number) - Required - Must contain exactly n items.
- **check(z.minSize(n))** - **n** (number) - Required - Zod Mini alias for .nonempty() when n=1; must contain n or more items.
- **check(z.maxSize(n))** - **n** (number) - Required - Zod Mini constraint; must contain n or fewer items.
- **check(z.size(n))** - **n** (number) - Required - Zod Mini constraint; must contain exactly n items.

### Request Example
```ts
z.set(z.string()).nonempty(); // must contain at least 1 item
z.set(z.string()).min(5); // must contain 5 or more items
z.set(z.string()).max(5); // must contain 5 or fewer items
z.set(z.string()).size(5); // must contain 5 items exactly
```

```ts
z.set(z.string()).check(z.minSize(1)); // alias for .nonempty()
z.set(z.string()).check(z.minSize(5)); // must contain 5 or more items
z.set(z.string()).check(z.maxSize(5)); // must contain 5 or fewer items
z.set(z.string()).check(z.size(5)); // must contain 5 items exactly
```
```

### Enable zod/compile via Node.js --import CLI flag

Use the Node.js `--import` flag to guarantee `zod/compile` runs before any module defines a schema.

```sh
node --import zod/compile app.js
```

### Configure Zod in devDependencies for local development

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Add zod to devDependencies alongside peerDependencies to satisfy peer dependency requirements during library development.

```ts
// package.json
{
  "peerDependencies": {
    "zod": "^4.0.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "zod": "^4.0.0"
  }
}
```
